mapping.recorded_at: EntityEdge.created_at (REQUIRED field; add_episode sets wall-clock now; direct save/SET can carry the platform value)
mapping.superseded_at: EntityEdge.expired_at (add_episode sets wall-clock now at invalidation)

as_of_2023: Sarah Chen works at Acme as a software engineer
as_of_2025: Sarah Chen is an Engineering Manager at Acme

notes: Valid time maps cleanly: valid_at/invalid_at, and a backdated successor invalidates its predecessor at its own valid_at. RECORD time does not: add_episode stamps created_at/expired_at with wall-clock now, so evt_002 'recorded 2024-06-10' would read as today. Mitigation (ADR-017): the platform's Postgres fact table is the system of record for recorded_at/superseded_at and as_of/known_at; the graph projection carries valid_from/valid_to and, where cheap, overwrites created_at with the ledger's recorded_at after add_episode (shown to work). Formal bitemporal SLA stays out of MVP scope (DEC-12).
